annotation_description: Casting Sunpearl Kirin precombat before playing a land drop and before attacking with Spyglass Siren. They should play a land first (they have Gloomlake Verge and Godless Shrine in hand), then attack with Spyglass Siren for 1 flying damage, then cast Kirin post-combat to bounce the Map Token for a card draw.

message: Select up to one other target nonland permanent you control
annotation_description: Bouncing Spyglass Siren instead of the Map Token is suboptimal. Bouncing the Map Token would draw a card (since it's a token, the Kirin trigger says 'If it was a token, draw a card'), giving pure card advantage. The Siren can be replayed but costs mana and the Map token it creates on re-entry is the same as what's already on the board. Drawing a card for free is strictly better than re-buying a 1/1 flyer's ETB.

Attacking with Sazh's Chocobo as a 1/2 when Ba Sing Se could have been played before combat (it enters untapped since they control a basic Forest) to trigger landfall, making Chocobo a 2/3. As a 2/3, if blocked by Sunpearl Kirin (2/1), Chocobo would survive the block and kill the Kirin. As a 1/2, both creatures trade in a block.

message: Select up to one other target nonland permanent you control
annotation_description: Bouncing Sunpearl Kirin instead of the Map Token misses a free card draw. The ETB trigger says 'If it was a token, draw a card,' so bouncing the Map Token would have drawn a card for free while removing a relatively low-value permanent. Bouncing Kirin just returns a 2-mana creature to hand that needs to be recast.

Played a second Sunpearl Kirin instead of Kaito, Bane of Nightmares when the opponent was completely tapped out. Kaito would be a 3/4 hexproof creature during their turn that generates card advantage through surveil/draw and can stun opposing creatures. The opponent's tapped-out state made this the ideal window to deploy Kaito safely.

message: Select up to one other target nonland permanent you control
annotation_description: Bouncing a Map Token with Sunpearl Kirin draws a card since it's a token being returned. However, the player could have bounced Spyglass Siren instead, which would allow replaying it to create another Map Token (netting an additional Map Token). Bouncing the Map Token just draws a card but loses the token permanently since tokens cease to exist when returned to hand.

message: Choose spell or ability to playBa Sing Se
chosen_display: 2. {2}{G}, {T}: Earthbend 2. Activate only as a sorcery. (Target land you control becomes a 0/0 creature with haste that's still a land. Put two +1/+1 counters on it. When it dies or is exiled, return it to the battlefield tapped.)
annotation_description: Used all mana on Earthbend 2 to create a 2/2 hasty land, when playing Forest first and casting Mightform Harmonizer (4/4 with landfall) would have been far superior. Mightform's landfall from the Forest would double Surrak's power to 8, allowing an attack for ~14 damage (opponent at 16 → 2) versus only ~8 damage with the Earthbend line.

message: Select a creature an opponent controls
annotation_description: Grim Bauble's -2/-2 on Surrak (4/3) only temporarily reduces it to 2/1 without killing it, and triggers Surrak's draw ability giving the opponent a card. Targeting Llanowar Elves (1/1) or Badgermole Cub (2/2) would have killed them outright (still triggering Surrak's draw, but at least permanently removing a creature).

Opponent is at 1 life and Nature has 4 flying creatures (2x Sunpearl Kirin, 2x Spyglass Siren) that can attack for lethal unblocked since the opponent has no flyers. Casting Kaito precombat is completely unnecessary and wastes 4 mana when the game is already won by simply attacking.
